distractors.reason: 'Lazy work' describes poor effort or a person who does not want to work. It does not describe work that is not paid.
'Cheap' means low in price or low in quality. We don't use it to say that someone works without pay.
'Idle' means not working or not in use. 'Idle work' is not a natural phrase; we say 'idle time' or 'idle hands'.

example_sentence: Many teenagers spend their summer doing ___ work at a local animal shelter.
l1_interference: Osoby mówiące po polsku często tłumaczą 'bezpłatna praca' jako 'free work'. W angielskim, gdy mowa o pracy bez wynagrodzenia, mówimy 'unpaid work'.
explanation: In English, 'unpaid' is the adjective used for work that someone does without receiving money, such as volunteering. 'Unpaid' is the standard partner for 'work' in this sense.

related_collocations.example: She does voluntary work every Saturday at the library.
He got a summer job in a café.
Many students look for part-time work after school.

memory_tip: UNPAID = work with no money paid back to you (volunteering) | FREE = costs nothing for you to get, such as a free ticket
